newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela labor reform costs not in '98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela labor reform costs not in '98 budget.

text.p: Venezuela's proposed 11.2 trillion bolivar ($23.2 billion) 1998 budget does not include government payments due next year under a recent, ground-breaking labor reform, deputy Finance Minister Wilmer Perez said.

The payments, which total an estimated 980 billion bolivars ($2 billion) next year, were not included in the budget "because the labor reform had not passed Congress when the cabinet approved the budget," Perez told reporters in Congress.

The Labor Law reform, which paves the way for a revamping of Venezuela's crumbling social security system, was approved by Congress on June 10 and passed into law on June 19. The economic cabinet approved the 1998 budget on June 4.
"The second reason is that calculations of the total cost of the labor reform are still very rough," Perez said, adding the labor payments would be financed seperately.
Perez said the cost of moving Venezuela's one million public sector workers to the new fully-funded pension system, spread over five years, would total some 3.7 trillion bolivars.
The proposed 1998 budget forecasts a surplus equivalent to 1.34 percent of gross domestic product, versus an estimated 1.7 percent surplus for this year.
